articles.summaryOriginal: U.S. President Donald Trump unveiled South Korea’s U.S. investment projects in Washington on Wednesday, including a Texas gas-fired power plant, eight large-scale nuclear power plants and an Alaska LNG project. The announcement appeared to differ from Seoul’s position that only the Texas project has been finalized so far. US President Donald Trump makes an announcement with Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick in the Oval Office of the White House, Washington, Sept. 30. UPI-Yonhap

articles.summaryOriginal: Companies are expanding sports sponsorships into technology, training and long-term support. SK Telecom has backed Korean fencing for 24 years and used AI at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Hyundai Motor Group has supported Korean archery since 1985 with engineering-based training tools, while other firms are widening sports partnerships across multiple events. South Korean fencers celebrate with the national flag after winning the women’s team sabre final against Japan at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games at Aichi Sky Expo in Tokoname, Japan, Sunday. articles.summaryOriginal: Korea on Thursday protested a U.S. announcement on the Alaska LNG and nuclear reactor projects, saying it retains discretion over whether to invest. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said he raised the issue with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick after the White House presentation went beyond what had been agreed. Seoul said the projects remain subject to commercial reasonableness checks and domestic procedures. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan speaks during a briefing at Government Complex Seoul, Sept. 22. Courtesy of Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources

articles.titleOriginal: 120 meters above Seoul, slackliner stuns crowds
articles.titleJa: ソウル上空120メートルのスラックライナーで人を驚かせよう
articles.summaryJa: エストニア出身の3度のスラックライン世界チャンピオンであるJaan Rooseは、木曜日にソウルのダウンタウンから120メートル上空でパフォーマンスを行った。ソウル市が主催し、レッドブルが主催したこの公演は、ソウル中心部の上空で開催された初めてのスラックライン公演でした。
articles.summaryOriginal: Jaan Roose, a three-time slackline world champion from Estonia, performed 120 meters above downtown Seoul on Thursday. Sponsored by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and hosted by Red Bull, it was the first slackline performance held high above central Seoul. Roose said the city setting made the preparation difficult and called the performance a surprise and a miracle. Slackliner Jaan Roose walks a line 120 meters above Jung District, Seoul, Thursday, with the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin at Gwanghwamun Square in the foreground. Korea Times photo by Shim Hyun-chul
